What was real, and what was done. (1) A signature could freeze wording the supplier never saw (two findings, one fault): the page now sends the SHA-256 of the exact wording it rendered (the organisation's name filled in) with each signature, and Submit refuses with TEXT_STALE unless it is the hash of the wording read under the lock, which also catches a wording corrected in place under the same id and an organisation renamed after the page was drawn. The GIRO tick is made on step 4, so it is bound there: the draft stores the hash of the wording the box was ticked on, a save that ticks without naming the wording in force is refused, and a tick whose hash is no longer the wording in force no longer counts (the supplier is told the wording changed and ticks again). A tick that predates the column holds no hash and is void. Submit takes the organisation FOR KEY SHARE and the declaration texts FOR SHARE before reading them, and the configuration action that corrects a wording takes the organisation, then the row FOR UPDATE, then counts the signatures: one order everywhere (organisation, then the row), so a send and a correction or a retirement cannot wait on each other in a cycle. A wording is still corrected in place while nobody has signed it; with the hash that is safe, and a correction in flight is waited for. (2) BD-613-44 is wired (`payment/eligibility.ts` `creditorFaults`, `payment/creditor-store.ts`, `payment/at-issue.ts`): an interim certificate, and an advance payable to the main contractor, issue only to the supplier the award names on the register (`Award.vendorId`) when the latest CHECKED version of its creditor profile is in force; a newer sent version that is not checked leaves the earlier one in force; nothing checked refuses, saying whether nothing was sent, it waits for a check or it was found not in order; an award linked to no supplier is refused as that. (5) What the supplier is told of an officer's check: the officer's request remarks verbatim, and a bank change's reason (the profile's note is for the supplier by its own words); NOT the verification note of a document (the status words say they are never told), so a document not accepted with no request is told "send a corrected copy, or contact the office". (11) Eligibility lists only what the public may read (`isPublicOpportunity`) and is judged for the 30 that close soonest, saying how many are open; an invited exercise is not listed (My Bids, 4d). (13) The signature of a bank change is the creditor profile's `enteredBy` slot (a signature-class supplier slot); a wizard-sent version 1 carries none, as its signature is the application's, and `npm run auth:attribution` (persons' slots) reports nothing missing. (14) The supplier's own reading of its profile is logged as OWN_RECORD with its account as the actor, as 4b did. (15) The demonstration rewrites one existing row: demo_sx18's contractor requirement's words (with an audit row) so the eligibility view has a requirement that is compared; it adds every other row.

- 2026-10-09 · Phase 4d, decisions taken in the build (each the plan's honest default; the product owner may overrule). (1) A sign-up is NOT attendance. It is its own record (`SiteEventRegistration`), keyed by the event and the session's supplier, never by `ExerciseParty` (a party is linked to the register only by an officer's audited act), and it never writes `SiteEventAttendance`. The purchase gate (`attendanceFaults`) reads the officer's register only, so a supplier that only signed up is still refused on a mandatory event, and the pre-sale check says so in words; a database test pins it. (2) An acknowledgement is its own append-only record (`AddendumAcknowledgement`) and is allowed only where one of the supplier's linked parties holds a copy of the addendum. It never sets `AddendumRecipient.acknowledgedOn` or `despatchedOn`, which stay what an officer recorded of a paper copy. (3) The notices are the office's own records, read for the supplier's linked parties that bought the documents or were invited: addenda from `AddendumRecipient`, a closing change and a cancellation from the applied `ClosingChange` and `WindowCancellation` (not from `WindowNotice`, so a notice is shown whether or not an officer recorded a delivery row), and a notice of non-award. Seeing one is not delivery. (4) Own-bid status is the exercise's stage and whether the issued award is this supplier's, nothing else: before the opening nothing (6.6 OD-2: an envelope names no bidder before it), after it no price as read, no verdict, no score, no rank. A bid is shown only where the office has linked the bidder's party to the supplier, and the screen says that in words rather than "no bid". (5) A confidential (restricted) exercise is never in the open list or public; a supplier reaches it only through a party the office linked to it, with its window published, and every other id reads as not found, alike for an id that exists nowhere (`supplierSees`, pinned). (6) The inspection log is written first, in its own transaction, and the content is read only after it commits; only the approved, frozen version is shown (a watermarked draft is refused); the closing changes and addenda issued since approval are said beside the text, as on the officers' print (the supplier must not read a stale closing as the closing); a refusal is not logged. (7) A request for the documents records the checks as judged. A request the checks stop is kept as a refused attempt with its reasons (FR-ADV-010: "refused with the reason recorded") once, never again for the same refusal; where the only thing in the way is that the sale is not open, nothing is refused or recorded. A request starts no sale: an officer records the sale as at the counter, and the request reads as sold when a sale to the supplier stands. (8) `electronicDocumentRelease` is a nullable Boolean on `WindowPolicy` with provenance: unset releases nothing and says so (not the same as off); on, the pack is shown only while a sale to the supplier stands, its finance receipt number is recorded by an officer and the window is between publication and the closing, and each opening is logged. (9) The notice of non-award is a separate officer act on the award page (`beginAct`, slot `NonAwardNotice.issuedBy`); the award's own issue is untouched. It refuses while `AwardPolicy.nonAwardNotices` is unset or "no", naming policy D7; carries a reason only where `debriefIncludesReason` is true (unset: none, whatever was typed); never carries a score, a rank or a figure; is frozen as issued; one per tenderer per exercise. The unsuccessful tenderers are the parties named on an opened bid other than the awardee; an award that names no awardee party issues nothing and says so. (10) Locks: a supplier's act locks the exercise and then its window and never the supplier row (`recordSale` takes the supplier row last), pinned by `supplier-reach.test.ts`. (11) The print view's article was moved into a shared component (`src/components/tender-document.tsx`) so the supplier's inspection and the officers' print read alike; the text of both print pages is unchanged (a before and after snapshot).

- 2026-10-09 · Phase 4e, decisions taken in the build (each the plan's honest default; the product owner may overrule). (1) A contract is the contractor's to open in one way: its award names the supplier on the register (`Award.vendorId`, the officer's audited link that a payment certificate already needs) and the award is ISSUED or ACCEPTED. A draft or pending award, a cancelled award and an unlinked award open nothing, and every other id reads as not found, alike for an id that exists nowhere (`supplierHoldsContract`, pinned). The exercise's confidentiality is not consulted: the awardee is a party to its own contract. (2) A submission is NOT a record on the contract. It is the contractor's own row, frozen as sent, and the officer records what it calls for (the programme's points, the valuation, the delay notice) through the existing act; the answer "taken up" says so. A submission of every kind is judged under the SUPERVISION row of the act × status table (allowed from numbering through making good complete, so a defects report and the statutory declaration are allowed after practical completion), and refused on a cancelled, terminated or closed contract in the table's words. (3) The service level is calendar days from the day sent (ASSUMED calendar; the governing documents give none), per kind, unset by default; unset means no due day and never "overdue", and the queue, the configuration and the contractor's list all say so in words. The level and the due day are frozen on the submission when sent. (4) Routing is to the S.O. office in force on the contract on the day (the same `soOfficeOn` the officers' acts use); the office's label is kept on the row, its holders and those acting in it are told once each by a staff notice carrying the kind and the contract and never the amount, and a contract with no S.O. assigned is routed to nobody, said on the row and in the contractor's Overview. (5) Who may answer: the S.O. office's holders (or those acting in it), or a representative whose delegation letter lists contractor communication, judged today through `recorderFaultToday` with the need `{ act: "CONTRACTOR_COMMUNICATION" }`, as the officers' own communication acts are; the answer is the signed-in officer's own act (`beginAct`, `onBehalf: false`), once, and an administrator is refused. (6) Three acts are signatures with the password: the statutory declaration (the one kind the store attributes on `ContractorSubmission.submittedBy`; the other kinds are plain submissions, the column the record and the audit row the proof), the agent's attestation, and the contractor's block or refusal on a certificate. A disagreement on the diary is words, not a signature: recorded with the account (`SiteDiaryEntry.disputedBy`, not an act slot). A stale or missing password entry refuses the act and the transaction rolls back; a database test holds it. (7) The officers' paper path stays: an officer can still record the agent's attestation and the contractor's block from paper, and each screen says which it was ("signed from the supplier portal" or "recorded from paper, not signed"). (8) The contractor's block is offered only on the two kinds the requirement names (VARIATION, SUM_ADJUSTMENT), only while the certificate is being signed, and only when it is the next block in printed order (the same `nextBlock` rule the officers' act follows); a dispute is the refusal the pinned form allows, and where the form does not allow one the contractor is told to raise it with the S.O. in writing. The contractor's signature can issue the certificate where its block is the last, as an officer's can. (9) The contractor reads its own contract sum and its own issued certificates' figures (the payment recommended, Finance's payment) with no SULIT gate and no access log: they are on the certificates the contractor holds and on the award published to it, and none is a registered SULIT field; the contract's priced working (estimate rates, corrections, override trails) is not read. (10) Announcements are shown to every signed-in supplier, applicants included ("visible to all registered vendors" is read as every account the office has activated); a withdrawn announcement is kept with its reason and never deleted or edited. (11) The permission is granted-only (`GRANT_ONLY`), so an administrator never publishes: the same direction as every act outside configuration, taken in the refusing direction. (12) Locks: a supplier's act takes the contract's canonical chain (`withLockedContract`; `withLockedCertificate` for a block) and never the supplier row; the act-status scan names the held-contract wrapper as an exception because every act inside it asks the table first.

- 2026-10-09 · Phase 5, step 1 (the machinery, the drafts of 5a, and numbering, evaluation and scope moved). (a) One mechanism for all of 5b. A Configuration editor's save is a `ConfigurationChange` of kind `CONFIGURATION_EDIT` (and the seven kinds of 5a, `QUORUM_CHANGE`, `OPENING_PANEL_SIZE`, `CLASSIFICATION_DOWNGRADE`, `BASELINE_CORRECTION`, `AWARD_TERM_CORRECTION`, `CONTRACT_DATE_CORRECTION`, `AWARD_RETURN_CORRECTION`, each its own enum migration `20261018090000` to `20261018090070`, BD-613-112). The payload names the editor (`numbering.saveSeries`) and holds what was posted; a password and an act's attribution fields are never stored (`isStoredField`), a file up to 1.5 MB is (the logo is 512 KB). The editor itself is the section's `core.ts`, untouched but for moving; `actions.ts` is only the proposal. The editor runs twice, by `src/lib/auth/edit-store.ts`: as a REHEARSAL at the proposal, with everything undone, which tells the proposer the editor's own refusals beside its own fields and keeps the audit rows it wrote as the change's `before`, read to the second person in History's words (a value held SULIT is not shown, `describeEdit`); and FOR REAL at the decision, inside the decision's transaction. It is applied only if the audit rows it would now write name the same records, actions and `before` values; otherwise the change is STALE, written, and nothing applied. Only the fields an edit moves are compared, so a serial that advanced does not make a series' pattern change stale. (b) How the editors keep using `db`: `db` is now a Proxy (`src/lib/db.ts`) that stands for the decision's or the rehearsal's transaction while an ambient one is set (`src/lib/ambient/ambient-tx.ts`, an AsyncLocalStorage on `globalThis`), and a `db.$transaction` inside is a SAVEPOINT, so an editor that catches a clash undoes only its own writes. `writeAudit` also captures its rows while one is set. This is the one change to a shared module; `edit.db.test.ts` proves the rehearsal leaves nothing, the apply is one transaction with the decision, a throw undoes the whole decision, a caught clash undoes only itself, staleness, and the refusals. (c) Permissions: an edit is proposed by a holder of `configuration.draft` and decided by a different holder of `configuration.issue`, the approval matrix's pair (draft then issue). No new key (the list is closed, ruling 1664), nothing named for a role; an administrator holds both by the flag, so a database with one administrator and no granted role cannot change any configuration and says "a second person is needed" (the demonstration has two administrators). An editor that reaches what an administrator is kept from is marked `administratorMay: false` in its section's `operations.ts`: an administrator then neither proposes nor decides it, and is not counted among those it waits for (none is marked yet; the 5a corrections are). (d) The lock order of an edit is the change's own row and then whatever the editor locks, in its own order; the organisation's row is not taken first, because an editor that locks another row before the organisation would be ordered against every path that does (`lock-order.test.ts`). (e) The drafts of 5a (the plan's "versioned items"): an evaluation model and a rate schedule are drafted by their maker (`configuration.draft`; every accepted edit writes `ConfigurationDraftMaker`, a refused one does not) and issued by someone who is not a maker, who holds `configuration.issue`, with the password for a model (`EvaluationModel.issuedBy`, a signature-class slot an administrator may do, as the matrix's) and as built for a schedule (`RateSchedule.issuedBy`, still refused to an administrator account, ruling 1849). The database holds it: trigger `guard_draft_issue` (SQLSTATE PA005; migration `20261018100000`) refuses a draft put into force with no issuer, no maker on record, or by a maker, and an issuer changed afterwards; a row written already in force (a loader's history) is not judged. A draft that has no maker on record (one that existed when this landed) is issued by no one until someone adopts it (`adoptModelDraft`, `adoptRateDraft`, with a reason) or edits it. The demonstration's evaluation models are written already in force, with no issuer, as a model issued before sign-in is (a placeholder snapshot that the loader replaces in the same run, because a row in force must carry one). Templates and forms have no draft and issue of their own (an edit bumps `bodyVersion`), so they are issued by a non-maker by being proposed and applied: they move with 5b. (f) The screens: a save that is a proposal keeps its drawer open and says so in place of its fields ("Proposed. Nothing has changed yet ...", `FormState.notice`); every Configuration page shows, to a maker, a checker and a reader of the audit trail, how many saves wait for a second person, with a link to Changes waiting; the queue reads an edit in the trail's own words. (g) Tests changed deliberately, each at the plan's 5b line: `numbering-scan.test.ts` and `lock-order.test.ts` read the numbering editor in `core.ts` (the same code, the same lock, only the file moved), `permit-list.test.ts`, `config-locks.test.ts` and `act-attribution-scan.test.ts` read the scope editor in `core.ts`, `two-person-scan.test.ts` names `edit-store.ts` as the second writer of `ConfigurationChange`, `configuration-change.test.ts` now expects a holder of `configuration.draft` to read the queue (they make edits), `auth-reach.test.ts` names `stageEdit` as a guard (pinned in `registry-scan.test.ts`: its first await is `staffForPermission("configuration.draft")`) and lets Configuration's layout read the count after `requireStaff`, `act-slots.test.ts` and `act-wiring-scan.test.ts` add `EvaluationModel.issuedBy`. (h) OPEN for the product owner, each taken as the default shown. (1) An act an editor begins while it is applied (a delegation's "Granted by") is the applier's own: the person a form names is data of the record, not an attestation, because only the proposer could have made one and the proposer's own is the proposal (`ConfigurationChange.proposedBy`). The alternative is a new attribution mode that names the proposer as subject and the applier as recorder; it needs an enum migration and changes every reader of attribution. (2) An editor that does more than write its record (marking a person away sweeps their pending steps and tells their superior) is rehearsed as the proposer and run as the applier, so where the sweep reaches different steps the change reads as STALE: conservative, and the proposer proposes it again. (3) A proposal with no reason is allowed where the editor does not ask for one (as the direct save was); the editors that ask for one still do, because they are rehearsed. F1 (the browser chooses who acts): a proposal's maker is the session's actor (`proposedBy` is read from the session in `stageEdit`, never from the form), the decider is read the same way, and the difference of the two is held by the pure rule, the action and the existing decision trigger, so a forged `personId` field changes nothing; the one field a form does carry for an act (`personId` of an attribution) is checked against the session by `beginAct` as before. Threats considered that the plan did not list: a stored payload is a place a secret could rest, so a password and an act's attribution fields are never stored, a SULIT value is withheld from the second person (`describeEdit`), and a payload is capped (600 fields, 200 KB a value, 1.5 MB a file); a decision made on a stale record is refused, not applied (`editIsStale`); and an edit applied by the machinery cannot name a subject (`namesSubject` false) so it cannot be used to put words in another person's mouth. - 2026-10-09 · Phase 5 rulings applied (the round of log line 2048). 1982(h)(1), the delegation's grantor: when a second person applies a delegation, the attribution of "Granted by" names the person the form names, and is made through the PROPOSER (`beginActAmbientWith` and `beginActAppliedWith` in `src/lib/auth/act-begin.ts`; the app's `beginAct` is that function). The proposer comes from the change's own row (`Ambient.proposer`, set by `decideEdit`), never from a form. If the form names the proposer, the row is SIGNED by them (their own act, made at the proposal; the slot is not a signature, so no password) and the applier is on the change as its `decidedBy`. If it names another person, the row is RECORDED_ON_BEHALF with the proposer as recorder and the paper reference and reason the proposal kept. The stored proposal now keeps `<person>:paperReference` and `<person>:reason` (`isStoredField`); it still never keeps a password, `:onBehalf` or `:backdate*`. What the proposer was asked at the proposal (the permission to record from paper, `grantorFault`) was judged by the rehearsal and is not asked again of the applier (`JUDGED_AT_PROPOSAL`, `appliedAttributionFaults`, `PreparedAct.appliedFromProposal`); every other rule is read again, and a signature is never applied. NO MIGRATION: the ruling allowed a new attribution mode only if one was needed, and none is. A recorder who is the proposer and a subject who is the grantor already fit SIGNED and RECORDED_ON_BEHALF, and the `ActAttribution` checks (a signed act is by its subject, an on-behalf act is for another) hold as they are. Every reader of attribution reads the two rows correctly as they stand ("Granted by X"; "Recorded by the proposer on behalf of X, not signed"), where a third mode would have changed all of them. The supplier list of types is the rules less the Office types (`supplierAcceptedTypes`), used by `loadUploadSettings` and `acceptNote`; if the rules list only Office types a supplier's upload reads as closed, and its words now say "from suppliers". (7) The FR-ADV-010 "sighted" check online is a reading of the signed-in person's standing on the supplier record (`buyerStandingCheck`: an active portal account, a contact not retired from the supplier, the supplier's standing not barring the act), kept with the purchase; the register's reading of the supplier is the counter's. Reason: without the simulator, the only payer of an online purchase is an officer typing the finance receipt. A receipt typed against the wrong purchase gives documents and bid standing to a supplier who did not pay, and uses up the number, so the supplier who paid cannot be recorded and cannot tender. An officer proposes it with a reason; a different officer, not the one who recorded the receipt, approves it through an existing two-person pattern (the configuration change or the opening's dual authorisation; if neither fits, the ADR says why). It is allowed only while the window is open and no bid is held. It voids the sale and moves the purchase PAID to VOIDED, a new transition the trigger explicitly allows. A raw-SQL partial unique index keeps one live purchase per supplier and window, so the supplier can buy again. Where the reversal corrects a receipt typed against the wrong purchase, the number moves to the right purchase, which is awaiting payment, in the same audited transaction. The old value stays in the audit. The receipt's unique index (OD-11) and the counter's one-person void are unchanged. A voided counter sale keeping its number is a separate open point for the founder. The product moves no money. A refund reference is typed by an officer from finance, never generated; with none, the record reads "No refund recorded". Whether fees are refunded is the organisation's policy. A real provider's refund comes with its adapter (INT-10). Design 0003 ruling 17b.

(2) The register's restriction is read by its own closing-day reader (`readRestrictionForClosing`), not by the eligibility RESTRICTION row: that row judges the whole window from the advertisement day and would fail a document that starts after it, which is stricter than "in force on the closing day". (3) A document lodged after the closing day is not read at the opening, and a renewal lodged after the closing day does not hold a verdict: a late lodging does not rescue a bid. (4) An unset closing-day rule is a blocking fault only where it decides (the document expires on the closing day), not for every restricted online bid; an unset evidence type is always a fault. (5) At the purchase "in force today" means verified, started, not expired and not recorded as not applicable; a document expiring on the closing day with the rule false or unset warns. (6) The purchase's reading (reference, validity, warning) is kept in the purchase's own `checks`, as the buyer's standing is, and the sale register reads it from there (`onlineRestrictionOf`): no sale column was added. The reading is taken at purchase and not again at payment. (7) The re-read acts are the initial, a checklist answer, the verdict and the correction of what was read; finalising needs a verdict on every offer and a NOT_ASSESSED offer cannot have one, so the verdict is where the wait ends. The re-read updates the offer and every alternative of the same bidder together. (8) `CheckState` gains WARN (allowed, with something to do before the closing) so the buyer's screen can tell a warning from a pass. (9) Removed with `ONLINE_RESTRICTED`: the `restricted` input of `onlineSaleFaults` and `takeSaleModeFaults` (it had no other use). There was no separate refusal in the policy save: the three were taking the setting, publication and the purchase.
- 2026-10-12 · Review of ruling 17a (code review of 3619ee02 and c8931888), judgement calls. (1) The reading frozen on an opened bid now carries the supplier, the evidence document type, the closing-day rule as read and the closing time (`supplierId`, `evidenceTypeId`, `closingDayCounts`, `closingTime` on the JSON; no migration). A retake reads the register by that supplier, never through the sale, which stops reading as live when the deployment withdraws the simulator. A reading frozen before these were kept falls back to the sale's supplier, and where none can be found the bid is settled NOT_EVIDENCED with the reason SUPPLIER_NOT_FOUND, in words, rather than held for ever. (2) One opening judges every bidder under one document type and one closing-day rule: a retake, and a later bidder's first reading, take both from the first reading any bid of the opening froze. A part that was frozen unset (the closing-day rule null) is read from the live setting at the retake, so a rule the customer sets afterwards is not refused for ever; clearing the evidence type mid-opening changes nothing for a bid already read. (3) A retake runs only after the act has been judged able to proceed and never on a finalised opening. A verdict refused after a retake wrote keeps the new reading (it is audited on the offer, as the ruling asks of every act) and the refusal says so, instead of "Nothing was saved". The alternative to an offer is audited with the reading's words, as the offer is. (4) A lodging counts at the opening if its organisation day is before the closing day, or is the closing day and it was recorded by the closing time (`recordedAt`, which is the moment the system took the lodging: `lodgedOn` is always that moment's organisation day and is never back-dated, so the two cannot disagree). (5) The purchase is read again when it is paid, by both writers of paid, on the supplier row the payment already locks; a document no longer in force refuses the payment in words (the buyer's on the simulator, the officer's on a receipt). The structured reading is frozen on the sale as `eligibilitySnapshot.restriction`, beside the register's own reading, and the restriction (a warning included) is in the trail of the sale and of the purchase. The sale register speaks in the staff's words from that reading. A sale paid before it was kept says only that it was verified when the documents were bought. (6) The purchase's warning is taken from the opening's own reading of the closing day over the documents an officer has checked, so a verified renewal that starts later but covers the closing day removes the warning, a renewal still waiting does not, and the words then say the waiting renewal must be verified, not lodged. An expired document with a renewal already waiting is refused in words that do not tell the buyer to lodge one. (7) "NOT_ASSESSED" says a renewal only where what waits is one; the verdict's refusal and the offer's label use words true of a first lodging too.

The CFRG entry exists: `test-vectors.json` from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cfrg/draft-irtf-cfrg-hpke/master/test-vectors.json (fetched once, SHA-256 61fc662f01996cd06d713dacf5e133167bd309a1f329442d53f1e21a47b3ede6, 128 entries) holds mode 0, kem 0x0020, kdf 0x0001, aead 0x0002 at index 4; it and the AES-128-GCM entry (index 0, RFC 9180 A.1, whose printed values it carries) are vendored byte for byte and their file hashes pinned in `hpke.test.ts`. Judgement calls: (1) The other vectors (RFC 7748, 5869, 7914 and the McGrew-Viega GCM cases) were transcribed from the published texts, since nothing else might be fetched; each transcription was checked against Node's independent primitives before it was written down, and the one that disagreed (RFC 7748 section 5.2's second single-step vector, transcribed with a digit missing) is left out rather than taking its value from the implementation under test; the iterated vectors cover the same function. RFC 7914's fourth vector (about 1 GiB) is above the module's 256 MiB cap and is not run; GCM cases 17 and 18 use other IV lengths and are excluded. (2) A private X25519 key is imported as PKCS#8 DER (the fixed prefix and the scalar), because Node's JWK import of a private OKP key requires the public `x` being derived; public keys go in and every key comes out as JWK. (3) `unwrapKey` throws SealError("PEPPER") for any pepper that is not the wrap's, including a pepper passed for a wrap made without one, so a caller must pass exactly the wrap's: it can never return null, so it can never be counted as a wrong passphrase. (4) The passphrase is read in Unicode normal form C, so the same text typed on another keyboard is the same passphrase. (5) A wrap's scrypt parameters are bounded (log2N 1 to 20, r 1 to 32, p 1 to 16, within the 256 MiB cap) and refused as FORMAT otherwise, so a forged row cannot make the server spend without bound. (6) `hpkeOpen` and `gcmOpen` are defined only in `open.ts`; the module's own openers are named apart and never imported from outside it (`open.test.ts`). (7) X25519 clamps bits 0 to 2 of byte 0 and bits 6 and 7 of byte 31 away, so a share altered only there gives the same key and the same public key; the test shows this as well as the refusal of a non-clamped flip. (8) `types.ts` keeps the §1.1 types as written and re-exports the implemented functions; `contract.test.ts` holds each to the plan's signature, written there as the plan has it.

- 2026-10-13 · Wave 3b stage A fix round, the triggers (migration `20261103200000`; security audit 1-5 and 7, review M1 and S3, ruling 20aa). Judgement calls: (1) Every sealed trigger function is replaced with `SET search_path = pg_catalog, public, pg_temp` and its tables named in `public`; the repository's other 22 trigger functions get the same `search_path` by `ALTER FUNCTION`, their bodies unchanged. Naming `public` assumes the product's one schema (DATABASE_URL `schema=public`, which every migration's unqualified DDL also assumes); a deployment in another schema would need these names changed. `db:roles` now revokes TEMPORARY on the database from PUBLIC as well as from the app's role, so every login of that database but the owner loses temporary tables. (2) "Written in this transaction" reads `xid8` columns that only triggers write (`insertedXact` on BidEnvelope, OnlineBid and PublishedKeyChange; `statusXact` on OnlineBid; `unsealedXact` and `finalisedXact` on Opening). They are `Unsupported("xid8")?` in the schema, because Prisma cannot create a row with a required unsupported column; the triggers set them on every insert, so NULL appears only on rows written before the migration, and reads as "not this transaction", which is true of each. A writer's value is overwritten, as the late flag is, and an ONLINE envelope's `insertedXact` cannot be changed (PA012). PublishedKeyChange is append-only, so its `xmin` could not be reset, but it takes the same column so no trigger reads `xmin` at all. (3) The rule that each ONLINE envelope has its OnlineBid at the commit (deferred, PA013) means no test or act may write an envelope alone; the trigger tests that did now write a submission with it, citing audit 2. (4) One standing bid per supplier per exercise (audit 7, S1, PA027) is a deferred constraint trigger, not an EXCLUDE constraint: the scratch database already holds test rows that break it, and an EXCLUDE constraint cannot be added NOT VALID. It takes an advisory lock on the supplier and the exercise and counts in a fresh statement, which sees a rival that committed while it waited only at READ COMMITTED, so it refuses any stricter isolation; step 10's submit and replace run at the default (noted in the plan). Alternatives are not limited. (5) "Published", for the channel and rules freeze (audit 4, PA025), reads the exercise's own status (ADVERTISED, INVITED or after), not the window's `publishedAt`, which the publish act writes before the status; so step 8 writes the pins before, or with, the status move (noted in the plan). The bid rules are also frozen once written, before publication too, since they are written only at publication. (6) The ShareRelease insert check (audit 5, PA026) also checks UNSEAL releases (the opening and the authorisation are of the key's exercise, the officer keys too) and that a release is written unused; a substitution is refused at or after the closing (`clock >= closing`), as `rosterChange` refuses the roster change itself. (7) Residual, not changed: a submission may still be written naming as replaced a live submission that the same act does not move to REPLACED. It gains nothing (the old one can never later be marked REPLACED by it, audit 2), but a deferred check could refuse it outright; left for the architect's review.

BUSY writes no row (it is judged before the exercise is known, and a row per refusal is what 20w forbids). (3) The upload contract has no CANCELLED fault, so a cancelled exercise answers NOT_PUBLISHED (not open for bids) and an exercise whose frozen mode is unset at the door answers ONLINE_NOT_ALLOWED; the contract is not widened. (4) The additional data of a file's three ciphertexts is written once, in src/lib/sealing/file-seal.ts: recordId is the file's id (made in the app before sealing) and partKey the returned part's id, for FILE_BODY, FILE_META and FILE_DEK alike. The stored body is ct then tag with the IV in bodyIv; the metadata is iv, ct, tag (packGcm); the sealed data key is enc then ct (packHpke). Step 13's unseal must rebuild them with fileBodyAad, fileMetaAad and fileDekAad. (5) Product constants in limits.ts (20e): 30 part uploads a minute per account; a body must arrive within 300 seconds and, after a 10 second grace, at no less than 16 KB a second (408 BODY_TOO_SLOW otherwise). The deployment's limit on uploads at once is the bid limiter (BID_UPLOAD_MAX_CONCURRENT), separate from the staff documents' one; the supplier's one place is per process, and the draft cap, judged again in the transaction under an advisory lock on the supplier and the exercise, is what holds across processes. (6) The form is read in memory by the runtime's multipart parser and its File cannot be zeroed from here; the one copy this route makes is zeroed, and the data key is zeroed by sealFile. Nothing plain is written to disk by us. The filename is sealed in the metadata only (cut at 255 characters) and appears in no audit row or event. (7) Unknown form fields, a repeated field and an upper-case browser hash are refused (the rule compares the hash exactly). (8) Discarding a draft already discarded answers ok and writes nothing; a file a submission took answers 409 and writes a REFUSED event; the sealed bytes of a discarded draft stay in the store (a ciphertext is never deleted). No migration was needed. (10) Found and fixed: hpke.ts read X25519_KEY_BYTES into a module constant at load, which is undefined when x25519 is the first of the sealing modules a process imports (types.ts re-exports both); sealing then failed with LENGTH. NENC is now the literal 32, pinned by import-order.test.ts. (11) The staff document upload now calls the shared recogniser (recogniseFile in media.ts) instead of its own copy of the sniff and the archive reading. - 2026-10-14 · Wave 3b step 9 follow-up: (1) The audit rows of a part's upload and discard now write words, not enum codes (scan and state), beside the ids and the cipher digest. (2) The claim that nothing outside the bid part reads a ScanResult was checked by grepping every call of the scanner: the configuration pages read only `configured`, and the one `.scan(` call is runScan. (3) PO question, a deployment fact the step cannot change: src/proxy.ts runs on every route, and Next then clones and buffers a request body in memory before a route handler reads it, up to `experimental.proxyClientMaxBodySize` (10 MB by default, truncating past it with a logged warning). So (a) a bid part larger than the buffer would arrive truncated and be refused as unreadable or as a hash mismatch, and the product's ceiling for one file (DOCUMENT_MAX_BYTES) and a part's maxBytes must stay under it or the setting be raised in next.config.ts (a change that needs a restart); (b) the route's deadline and minimum rate judge the buffered clone as it is handed on, which still bounds how long a handler holds its slot, but the wire speed of a slow client is seen by the platform and the reverse proxy in front of it, whose read timeouts are the deployment's to set (docs/notes/sealed-bids-deployment.md). The registration and Company uploads live with the same fact. Not fixed here.

(3) `needsAdmission`, `lateMatterFault` and the new `admittedEnvelopeIdsOf` (one filter shared by `gate-read.ts` and `opening/repo.ts`) treat SUPERSEDED as WITHDRAWN: nobody waits for an admission of a bid that no longer stands. The officer's withdraw and alternative-parent pickers no longer list online envelopes. (5) The audit mask is applied to the Configuration › Audit export (its only view of rows) and to the exercise History, after the evaluation-blind mask; NAMED_OFFICER is an ExerciseOpeningOfficer of that exercise not taken off, `unsealed` and `finalised` are the exercise's MAIN opening; a record whose exercise is not found is withheld. A changed row counts in the export's held-back figure. (6) The identity-column scan (sealed.test.ts) pins which files read the online tables: the step 10 stores and step 11's own-screens store may select identity columns, `audit-scope-store.ts` and `sealing/store.ts` name none. (b) `lateMatterSubject` ("Admission of late envelope N") and the audit label of the tabling name a late online envelope by its true sequence, possibly before the start, while the register shows its ordinal. Late bids are few, but it is the same leak. Should the matter name it by ordinal before the start? (c) The mask's unsealed and finalised flags are per exercise, judged on the MAIN opening. After the main opening is finalised, an admitted late bid (opened at a supplementary opening later) or a not-admitted one would show its supplier to everyone while it is still sealed or for ever. The conservative reading judges each late bid by its own opening. Should the mask do so once step 13 gives a supplementary opening its unseal? - 2026-10-15 · Step 14, the officer's download (`POST /api/opening/sealed-file`, internal copy only): order is guard, parse, the account's rate counted, opening and hidden-exercise check, administrator, roster, `downloadFaults`, the sign-in password through `beginActFrom` (the route twin of `checkUnlock`), the passphrase through `unlockOwnKey` (widened to log under kind DOWNLOAD), then the grant, body and metadata. Judgement calls: (1) "stream the file" is read as send it once every GCM tag and the plain digest and size have verified, because unverified plaintext must not leave; the file is held in memory (bounded by the download limiter, as the document download). (2) The rate is counted before anything is looked up or tried, keyed by the staff account, so a flood of refusals writes one row a minute (20w) and password or passphrase guessing is bounded; the limit (20 a minute, action `officer-sealed-download`) is a product constant with its reason in `limits.ts` (20e), not customer policy. (3) The grant is opened with the use written as the literal OPENING_CHECK, never read from the row, so a FINALISE grant cannot open here even if its column were changed. (4) A bid not opened at THIS opening (replaced, withdrawn, late and not admitted) reads as NOT_OPENED whatever its row says. (5) After the passphrase the opening is re-read, and a finalise that landed in between refuses. (6) The served media type is the sealed metadata's if the product recognises it, else application/octet-stream. (7) A request refused before the session (not signed in, cross-site, wrong content type) writes no row (20w); an unknown opening writes none either, having no exercise to attach to. (8) The Grand Summary exception needs no code of its own: it is a part whose frozen rule says openingCheck, and `grantPlan` already makes its grant OPENING_CHECK. Product-owner question: the Opening page has no download button yet (step 14 lists only the route); should steps 15 to 17 add one beside each bid's opening-check files, and should the page ask both the password and the passphrase in one form?

A permission refusal says what blocks it, then who can act. A validation refusal names the rule breached plus its source, and the citation does not count toward the 12 words. Product codes (FR-, NFR-, AC-, OD-, BD-, B1–B8, D1–D7, build-module numbers) never reach a screen. A customer's configured clause citation is data, not a code. It stays visible as "rule label · clause" at every decision point with a legal consequence: an approval step, a routing "Rule" row, the award approval, a validation refusal. It is never moved into a popover there. This replaces 0005 §3.2 rule 4. The code lint matches literal product-code patterns only, with a fixture test showing that money, percentages, dates and interpolated clauses pass.
- 2026-10-19 · Product owner (for the founder): minimal words, R3 (AGENTS.md rule 2). An assumed route, a route not checked against the matrix, or a role that resolves nobody keeps a `warn` callout of 15 words or fewer at the step where someone acts on it. Elsewhere it shows as an Assumed or Not checked chip.
- 2026-10-19 · Product owner (for the founder): minimal words, R4. The must-keep list grows by the following:
  - rule and clause at decision points;
  - the closing-date two-week rule when breached, and the newspaper-date warning;
  - alerts for bid validity expiry and insurance lapse;
  - each bid's comparison against the estimate in RM and per cent, and both variances and both classifications;
  - an assumed or unchecked route;
  - capability gaps shown as visible chips: Password only (MFA is not built; the NFR-SEC-005 code is removed), Restricted, Not scanned, Demo;
  - Not emailed, as a chip on staff screens and a visible line on the portal;
  - no payment provider, as a visible portal next step;
  - opening officers all needed;
  - no substitution after the closing;
  - the refused Office file: why, and what to save as instead;
  - a history that drops rows;
  - the expiry notification rule: none, off, or named;
  - every text a supplier or staff member signs, declares or attests to, kept verbatim. This includes evaluator conflict declarations, opening attestations and the Integrity Pact where it is shown.
- 2026-10-19 · Product owner (for the founder): minimal words, R5. An earlier ruling that required a sentence may become a chip with a popover, if the chip is visible where the ruling named it, uses 0005 §3.5's fixed words, and keeps its detail in a popover in the DOM. This covers provenance and Not set, Not judged, Not yet, return not set, and the 6.13 "says so" items. Warnings about a figure and all refusals keep a sentence within budget. The overclaim rulings (identity encryption, the ONLINE_SALE words, accepted file types) bind chips and popovers too: a shorter word may not claim more than the sentence it replaces.

InfoChip and MoreText meet WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.13 (dismissible, hoverable, persistent, keyboard-reachable), tested in step 0. A success notice goes away on the next action, never on a timer, and is never the only record of the act. 0005 §7 user testing is for the founder to run and is not a gate on the sweep. Each step's gate is §4's snapshot review.
